items.text: I am pleased to see that Ant’s new Claude Code has a version of background computer use on par with the version from Codex from last May this year. Nice work! Shipping great features first turns out to be a great way to encourage other labs to ship too. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to shipping. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go! We solved computer use in practice for GPT models about four months ago. items.title: Personal assistant agents are going to be a very exciting AI category
items.text: Personal assistant agents are going to be a very exciting AI category. It’s the first time you can have high token volume agentic use-cases that make sense for consumers. Lots of different approaches emerging right now, and it’s going to be hyper competitive because these agents will mediate a lot of consumer spend over time. But this certainly plays directly to Meta’s strengths: lots of compute required, can monetize with ads and commerce, software focused experiences so can distribute it at scale, and so on.

items.title: It's a weird time
items.text: It's a weird time. As many of you know, my superpower is optimism. I have an insane ability to look at any situation through the most positive lens. I strongly believe that today is the "least best" (not worst) day of my life and tomorrow will be glorious. I am super optimistic about where AI is going. But I also find myself genuinely anxious about the pace of change and our inability to understand how these (insanely) complicated machines work. I always err on the side of "just let us cook". The only way out is through. Let us build. But man, it is a weird time.

items.title: This kind of tweet is both interesting and misleading
items.text: This kind of tweet is both interesting and misleading. On the one hand, who doesn’t want a personalized vaccine that treats their cancer and reduces the need for chemo? On the other hand, there are many patients and families desperately looking for treatment. Presenting this as what cancer treatment looks like in 2026 is just not true: 1. Promising results in melanoma don’t mean personalized vaccines work across all cancers. 2. A treatment showing promise in a trial doesn’t mean most patients can get it or benefit from it.
